about: A video colour tool that can cut. Drive it with one command per line (the grammar below), observe it through `state print --json` (the model below) and the event stream, address any value with `set`/`get`/`eval`. Generated by `interstellar-cc api --json`; do not edit.

commands.summary: Create a project and its rack (an empty .cmp beside it), and open it.
Open a project: its timelines, and the hosted Cosmo project its #rack names.
Save the .isp and the rack's .cmp. A path saves the .isp there.
Close the project and return Home (its autosave goes: closing is a decision).
Write the autosave now — the .isp and every rack node's grade beside the project (<stem>.autosave.*); it happens by itself every `autosave` seconds while there are unsaved changes.
Put back an autosave newer than the project file (after a crash): the .isp and every grade, through Cosmo; the project is left unsaved so you decide. --discard removes the autosave instead.
The project's working space: Rec.709 (display-referred, Cosmo's own — the default) or ACEScct (scene-referred; the monitor and each render then apply an output transform).
Point the rack at an existing Cosmo project — its groups and grades are the rack.
Add photos or videos to the rack. A video is graded on a reference frame (`clip.mp4#t=2.0` picks it).
Group rack nodes — the named ones, else the selection; a group's grade stacks onto every descendant. No name: one is made up, as Cosmo does.
Duplicate a rack node as a variant: same media, its own grade.
Choose which frame of a video source Cosmo grades. Changes no parameter.
Change a rack node's bind name (what an address spells).
Make a rack node the Grade target and the selection. --add toggles it into the selection (Ctrl-click); --range selects from the last clicked node to it (Shift-click).
Take a source out of the rack (Cosmo's delete). Refused while a clip uses it.
Write addresses. A rack address writes THROUGH to Cosmo on a root timeline and becomes this version's override on a derived one.
Print an address's stored value.
Print an address's RESOLVED value in a timeline; --explain names every layer.
Drop this version's override at an address, so it inherits from its base again.
Create a timeline; with --base it is a version of that one (stores deltas only).
List timelines as a version tree.
Make a timeline the editor's current one.
Stop inheriting the base's colour: freeze it at a snapshot of the rack.
Inherit the base's colour live again.
Stop inheriting the base's arrangement: materialise the resolved cut.
Inherit the base's arrangement live again.
Report and prune dangling deltas; advance a pin to the rack's present state.
What this version changes relative to its base.
Delete a timeline. Refused while another version is based on it.
Add a track to the current timeline.

Place a span of a rack source — or of another timeline, nested (R-EDT-4) — on a track. Without --out, the rest of the source from --in (a still: 5 s; a timeline: to its last clip's end) — what a drag from the source bin drops. A timeline that would end up inside itself is refused.
Set a clip's source in and/or out point (seconds into the SOURCE, like `<clip>.in`); trimming the head keeps the remaining frames where they were on the timeline.
Cut a clip in two at a timeline time.
Move a clip in time and/or to another track.
Remove a clip; --ripple closes the gap.
Move the cut between a clip and its right neighbour.
Shift a clip's source range without moving it on the timeline.
Set a clip's playback speed.
Select a clip (none clears).
Add an image-processing plugin to a rack node's stack, after Cosmo and the node's other effects; prints its id (`ef_<n>`, stable for its life). Parameters are addresses: `set ef_3.radius=12`.
Remove a plugin from its node's stack.
Move a plugin to position <index> of its node's stack (0 = first after Cosmo).
Keep a clip — its source range, speed, geometry, opacity and blend — to paste.
Place a new clip from the copied one (default: at the playhead, on its track).
Dissolve between two adjacent clips; the outgoing clip is HELD through it.
Drop a named marker on the current timeline.
Attach a temporal effect to a rack node (footage) or a clip (editorial).
Remove a temporal effect.
Add an audio track (suite schema `#atrack kind=audio`).
Place a sound on an audio track: a file, or a rack source's own sound (`--src <bind>`). Without --out it runs to the end of the file's sound.
Step back one edit — a grade, an override, a cut, a version change — across the rack and the project alike.
Step forward again after an undo.
Copy a rack node's grade (its own params, masks excluded) to the clipboard.
Paste the copied grade onto rack nodes (or every source with --all). Root timeline only: it writes through to Cosmo.
Dissolve a group; its members keep their own grades.

Engine settings: cpuPercent (25|50|75|100), threads (0=auto), previewEdge (px), useGpu (0|1), uiScale (%), hardwareVideo (0|1: H.264/H.265 on the GPU's video unit), previewCache (0|1: build the graded preview cache when idle), keyLaneHeight (px, 80..600: the Cut key lane). Persisted; one CPU budget for the rack and the render path.
Apply a library preset to a rack source (the Grade target by default). Root timeline only.
Save a rack source's grade to the library as <name>.apf.
Copy an .apf (from Cosmo or anywhere) into the library.
Move the playhead; snapped to a frame.
Start playback of the current timeline.
Stop playback.

Queue a render of a NAMED timeline (no implicit current one), with its whole output spec: codec and profile, size (never above the project, same aspect), frame rate (the timeline is sampled at it), constant quality and encoder speed for H.264/H.265, bit depth for H.265, the output colour transform (HDR PQ/HLG need 10 bits; --peak is PQ's mastering peak in cd/m²). A flag the codec cannot honour is refused. dcp and imf write a folder (R-DLV-4): a SMPTE DCP (JPEG 2000 DCI X'Y'Z' fitted in its --container, 5.1 PCM) or an IMF App 2E package (JPEG 2000 RGB 12-bit, stereo PCM) — neither validated here, and the render says so.
Read an SRT's cues onto the open timeline as captions (timeline time, plus --offset); --replace drops the timeline's captions first. Styling tags are not kept. One undo step.
Write a timeline's captions (the open one unless named) as an SRT.
A caption on the open timeline: its words (\n is a new line) from --at for --dur seconds.
Remove a caption from the open timeline (a version drops the base's).
Show the caption under the playhead on the monitor, or not. Presentation; renders carry captions only with render --captions.
Cancel a queued or running render.

Save a render's whole output spec by name (beside the engine settings: every project has it); `render --preset <name>` applies it, flags given beside it winning. --res is a frame to fit in at the project's aspect.
Forget a saved render preset (the built-in ones stay).
The render presets: YouTube 1080p, ProRes HQ master and Review H.264 built in, then the saved ones.

Build the current timeline's graded preview cache now (a window also builds it when idle): one-second H.264 segments at the playing size, every frame checked by its plan, so only what an edit changed is rebuilt. Playback reads it; a render never does. `wait cache.done`.
Delete the current timeline's preview cache.

Add a keyframe to a parameter's curve (making the curve if it has none) — a rack node's colour key or an effect's parameter at a SOURCE time, a clip's opacity or geometry at a time on the clip's own footage clock. --at defaults to now on that clock (the source's reference frame; the playhead inside the clip), --value to what the parameter shows there. Root timeline only for the rack and effects: versions inherit curves (R-ANIM-5).
Remove the keyframe at --at (default now). The last one leaves the parameter animated with no keys (R-ANIM-10); what it showed stays.

Shape the keyframe at --at: move it (--to), change its value, its incoming/outgoing interpolation, speed (units per second) and influence (% of the segment) — After Effects' model; giving a speed or influence makes that side a bezier. --ease applies a preset.
Move several keyframes in time together, by --by seconds (one undo step) — a box-selection dragged in the graph. Refused when a key would land on another of its curve.
Copy keyframes (their values, shapes and sides, times relative to the earliest) to the key clipboard.
Paste the copied keyframes with the earliest at --at (default: now on each curve's clock) — onto the properties they came from, or onto --to when one property was copied. Same-time keys are replaced.

Mark a parameter to animate (R-ANIM-10) — its row appears in the timeline's ANIMATION section. offset (the default): Grade's value is the base and the keys are added to it, so a change in Grade moves the whole animation; it starts with no keys and changes nothing. fixed: the keys ARE the value, Grade's value now is the first key, and a change in Grade later does not touch the animation. A curve, a wheel or a crop is fixed.
Turn an animated parameter's curve into the other mode — its keys converted against the base so the picture does not change.
Remove a parameter's curve; the value it had now stays as the parameter's own.
Write one composited frame of a named timeline.
J/K/L: forward plays at 1×, then 2× and 4× on each press; back the same in reverse; stop pauses. Sound is heard at 1× forward only.
Set the timeline's In or Out at the playhead (or --at), or clear both; --source marks the source viewer.
Show a rack source in the viewer, with its own playhead and In/Out, for three-point editing; none = the timeline.
Move the source viewer's playhead (source seconds).
The video track Insert and Overwrite place on.

Three-point INSERT: the source (the viewer's, or --src) between its In/Out at the timeline In (or the playhead) on the target track; a clip there is split and everything after moves right on every track. Any three of source In/Out and timeline In/Out decide the fourth.
Three-point OVERWRITE: as insert, but what lies on the target track in the new clip's range is cut away and nothing moves.

A multicam: a new timeline with one video track per source (angle 1, 2, … in the order given), lined up by their timecode (default) or by their in-points (--in a=1.5,b=0.4 — source seconds, 0 when not given), and the sound of one source (--audio, default the first; none for silence). With --track, also placed on the current timeline at --at (else the playhead), showing angle 1.

Make a proxy of each named video source (none named: every one without a proxy) — ProRes Proxy (default) or H.264, its long edge --edge px (960 unless given), in <project>.proxies/ — as a background job like a render. The monitor uses it while `proxy use on`; renders never do.
Forget a source's proxy: the monitor decodes the original again. The file stays on disk.
The project's switch: the monitor (and playback, the preview cache, capture) decodes each source's proxy where it has one — or the originals. Renders and export-still always decode the originals.
List the offline sources in one place: each one's bind name, the file it names, and why it is offline.

Point a source at its file where it is now — `<source> <file>` (a CinemaDNG folder or pattern too), or --search <folder>: every offline source found there by its file name (a sequence by its folder). The grade, its history in this session and every clip stay; Cosmo keeps the slot it had. Refused, saying why, if the rack's structure changed since it was saved (Cosmo cannot save while a source is offline, D-2).

Grade's monitor shows the selected source's matte — where its grade reaches, white — instead of its picture: the key its qualifiers and windows (and its groups') make, so a key is pulled by looking at it.

Make a window follow what is under it: from the playhead's frame of its source, forward (or --back) to --to (else the source's end or start), the window's centre keyed on every frame where the patch it covers is found again. A background job, one frame per pump; one undo step.
Stop the running track; what it keyed stays (one undo step).

Keep what the monitor shows as a still, with the grade it was made with: a source's graded reference frame (named), or the timeline at the playhead with the grade of the clip on top there. Saved beside the project (<project>.stills/); the grade is a snapshot to apply, never an authority.
Apply a still's grade to rack nodes (else the Grade target) — through Cosmo, as grade paste writes; one undo step. On the root timeline (a version stores overrides).
Remove a still and its files.

Split the monitor between its picture and a reference — a still, or another version at the playhead — left | right (vertical) or top / bottom, the split at --at of the frame (0.5 unless moved). With no name, only the split moves. Presentation: renders and export-still never wipe.
Add a SERIAL node after a rack node: a new group around it, whose grade applies to its result — the rack's groups are the graph's serial chain.

Add a PARALLEL node to a source: a variant grading the same input beside it, its difference from the input added to the source's result by <variant>.parallelMix (1 unless set). It starts empty, so nothing changes until it is graded.
Remove a serial node (ungroups it) or a parallel node (removes the variant).

Switch the multicam clip under the playhead (or --at; --clip names it) to angle n FROM there: the clip is cut at that frame and the rest shows angle n — at its first frame, the whole clip does. One undo step.

Write a timeline for another editor: a CMX 3600 EDL (one video track, --track; reels and source timecode), FCPXML 1.9 or OpenTimelineIO — the format from --format or the extension. The record clock starts at 01:00:00:00 unless --start. AAF is refused, naming the way to it.

Read an EDL, FCPXML or OTIO into a NEW root timeline: its media added to the rack (found by path, or by clip/reel name under --media), its tracks, clips, dissolves and speeds. An EDL's rate is the project's unless --fps. Media that cannot be found is listed, not placed.

Bake a source's colour — its input transform and LUT, its grade as the open version folds it, its weight, its LUT effects — into a 3D .cube (33 points unless --size), optionally through an output transform. What is not per-pixel colour is left out and said so in the file.
Save what the monitor shows, at full resolution: --source names a rack source (its reference frame, graded — Grade); without it, the current timeline at the playhead.
Print the AppModel; --stable omits machine-dependent fields.
Print this document.
Report offline media, dangling deltas and refused fields.
Block (pumping) until a condition holds.
End a script or session.

events.name: info
events.summary: A note worth logging; carries no state.

events.name: error
events.summary: Something failed. Also set as AppModel.lastError.

events.name: command.rejected
events.summary: A line was refused (R-SVC-3): unknown verb, unknown flag, refused edit.

events.name: screen.changed
events.summary: Home / Loading / Edit.

events.name: project.opened
events.summary: A project is open.

events.name: project.saved
events.summary: The .isp and the rack's .cmp were written.

events.name: project.closed
events.summary: Back to Home.

events.name: rack.loaded
events.summary: The hosted Cosmo project finished decoding.

events.name: rack.changed
events.summary: A node was added, grouped, renamed, reframed.

events.name: params.changed
events.summary: An address was written. target = rack | version | clip | track | project.

events.name: selection.changed
events.summary: The Grade target or the selected clip changed.

events.name: timeline.opened
events.summary: The editor's current timeline changed.

events.name: timeline.changed
events.summary: A version was created, pinned, unpinned, frozen, thawed or deleted.

events.name: timeline.rebased
events.summary: rebase ran: deltas pruned, the dangling ones named, the pin advanced (old→new).

events.name: arrange.changed
events.summary: A cut operation landed.

events.name: playhead.moved
events.summary: The playhead moved by command.

events.name: playback.changed
events.summary: Playback started or stopped.

events.name: frame.ready
events.summary: A monitor frame was composited.

events.name: render.queued
events.summary: A render was queued.

events.name: render.progress
events.summary: Frames written so far.

events.name: render.finished
events.summary: A render completed.

events.name: render.failed
events.summary: A render stopped with an error or was cancelled.

events.name: lint.report
events.summary: Counts from `lint`; details follow as info.

events.name: history.changed
events.summary: An edit was recorded, undone or redone (did = edit | undo | redo | cleared).

events.name: settings.changed
events.summary: Engine settings after a change, all keys.

events.name: presets.changed
events.summary: The preset library was rescanned.

events.name: cache.changed
events.summary: The preview cache of the current timeline: frames cached and current, of total (R-PLAY-1).

events.name: keys.changed
events.summary: A parameter's curve changed; how many keyframes it has now (0 = no curve) (R-ANIM).

addresses.doc: White balance temperature, Kelvin. Group offsets stack by their offset from 6500.
Grain amount; seeded from (source, frame) so a render is reproducible (R-RENDER-2).
Master tone curve: control points `x,y[,ix,iy,ox,oy];…` in 0..1.
How far the mixer's hue selection reaches into the neighbourhood.
Source crop, normalised. Part of the look, one per source (R-FX-4).
Grade weight: a continuous bypass, blending ungraded→graded (R-RACK-4).
A parallel node's share: how much of its difference from the input is added to its source's result (R-CLR-3).
Reference frame a video source is graded on (R-RACK-3). Same as `rack frame`.
What the source IS: its input colour transform into the working space, before Cosmo grades it (R-COLOR-2). The media's interpretation, never a grade.
An input LUT on the source, after its input transform and before Cosmo (R-COLOR-5); `none` clears it.
Timeline position of the clip's first frame.
A multicam clip's angle: the placed timeline's video track it shows; 0 = all of it (R-EDT-5).
How the source fits the frame.
Balance: -1 left, +1 right; centre is unity.
Solo: while any track is soloed only soloed tracks sound.
How long they stay (more than zero).
The words; \n is a new line.
The plugin's output mixed over its input.
Gaussian Blur: Radius (source pixels; scales with the proxy).
Box Blur: Radius (source pixels; scales with the proxy).
